question: A user asks Claude to write a two-sentence reply to a coworker's Slack message. Claude responds with the two sentences directly in the conversation rather than opening a side panel. Why did this response not trigger an artifact?
options: A) Artifacts are disabled by default and must be manually enabled for every conversation, preventing side panel opening for any content.
B) The content is short and conversational, not substantial or self-contained text typically exceeding 15 lines.
C) Research mode must be active for an artifact to appear, and short conversational replies do not automatically enable this mode.
D) Two-sentence replies are only supported when composing within a Project's knowledge base, not in standard chat conversations.
correct_answers: B) The content is short and conversational, not substantial or self-contained text typically exceeding 15 lines.
explanations: Incorrect. Artifacts are enabled by default and appear based on content length and complexity, not a manual per-conversation setting. Short replies simply do not meet the threshold for triggering an artifact.

Correct. Artifacts are designed for substantial, self-contained content, typically over 15 lines, that users may want to modify or reference later. A brief two-sentence reply is short and conversational, so it stays inline rather than opening a side panel.

Incorrect. Research mode and artifacts are separate features; activating research mode is not required for an artifact to appear. Short, conversational replies do not generate artifacts regardless of whether research mode is on.

Incorrect. Two-sentence replies are standard in any chat conversation and are not restricted to Projects' knowledge bases. The content's length and self-contained nature—not the conversation type—determine artifact creation.
